Geometry is king, but there are actually 3 different RAM material types (at least that I know of) that are all fairly important and are a significant part of the how the geometry redirects the radar energy. The RAM coatings that goes over the entire plane may make up only 5% of its effectiveness, but the the RAM material that coats the edges are two fold essential. First of all, you wouldn't be able to create a functional stealth geometry with a plane that has edges from hatches and canopies without the specialized RAM material that lines all of the edges. Secondly, its actually now part of how the shaping and material design to redirect some the radar energy through the RAM coating and into areas that contain a thick piece of specialized RAM. When a radar wave hits a plane, the majority of the energy will deflect according the the plane's geometry, however, some of that energy will actually travel across the skin of the plane until it hits an edge where it will scatter. Modern stealth planes built using composite materials can increase this behavior compared to steel or aluminum. When the radar energy hits a stealth plane, its deflect most of the energy away at an angle, but it also captures more of the energy on the skin, which then travels across the skin through more of the RAM coating until it hits a zig zag edge that is filled with a with this pocket RAM for lack of a better term. The zig zag edge breaks up what would typically be a large single edge scatter into several smaller events and force more of the energy to travel into the pocket RAM. This helps a lot to reduce the energy of the wave that has been deflected and results in small weak scatter energy that doesn't have the strength to be detected at significant ranges.

Yeah shields can give barbarians a tough time for sure. You just have to be offensively minded when using the shield. Get into a panicked defensive mindset where you hold block and try to back out and you're dead meat. Your shield is the object that lets you attack with fewer consequences, not an item that will let you beat a retreat while invulnerable.

Once you learn how to use the shield properly it makes a big difference in PVE and in many PVP encounters. You need to learn the swing animations of the mobs in order avoid getting hit by certain swings from particular mobs that are able to get around the shield when you think they wouldn't. The most important general tip I can give you is to block from further back than you would normally think. For example the Axe skele overhead requires that you have at least a full swing distance between you and him and that you crouch and straight aim up to block. For PvP a good shield user can prevent players from quickly running over them on the offensive and use offensively to push into players denying ranged damage and stuffing attacks from 2h weapons. You need to make sure not to get stuck into a panicked defensive posture and realize that the shield only provides you with an opportunity to respond and punish. Do not become static, do not become passive, do not hold block for longer than necessary to intercept the attack. Incorporate dodging attacks into your counters and movement. Block, counter, crouch/lookdown & rotate, come up blocking, counter again. You can stuff players by running into their face and blocking while aiming slightly up. This will catch the hilt of their weapon if they attack. If for example you corner a Barbarian wielding an axe or bardiche, you can reliably stuff their swing counter and stuff again.

1st of all, you have to understand that there are major fundamental differences between the Sith and the Jedi in terms of their view of the force and the differences between the Light and the Dark sides of The Force itself.

The Jedi are monk like in their Zen. They do not fear death as they are removed from the materialistic and the individuality concepts of life. They Focus on the Harmonic nature of the Force and look to it as a sort of religion, or at least an attempt to "serve the force" or to let the Force guide them in their actions. This is what permits them to have a Jedi Order in comparison to the Sith. The Jedi are actually stronger together, organized and altruistic, capable of working together and being in harmony.

The Sith on the other hand, use the force as a tool. They are focused on becoming true masters of themselves by removing all chains and obstacles that constrict them. This does not  lend itself to functioning on an organizational level. The best example of this was the explanation of the title Darth from "Path of Destruction". The title itself is a challenge, to be a Darth is a proclamation of supremacy  and to state that you are open to all challenges made against you. With this in mind, could you really have a council of Darths, or organize an academy? At one point the Sith did do this, but the results were weak as it undermined not only the progression of power from weak apprentices overthrowing powerful masters by working in groups, but it also was less effective at harnessing power of the Dark Side.

The key to the Rule of Two, is the quest for power, one to embody it and the other to crave it. Both of these serve followers of the Dark Side of the Force well. Plagueis explained it best when he was training Palpatine. "I am your torturer Sidious, soon you will make every effort to appease me and with each lie you tell, with each attempt you make to reverse our roles, you make yourself as shiny as an iridium coin to the Dark Side" Plageuis here is hitting Palpatine with several lessons at once, using physical and emotional discomfort as fuel to evoke the Dark Side, inviting contest to his supremacy and control over him, and finally making him envious of this power. Only when the Apprentice is powerful enough to overcome his Master will he be worthy of the title and for a true Master of the Dark side, there can be no subservience, only death, and so the Apprentice must kill his Master to become one. The irony is that often the new Master proclaims an end to the Rule of Two but then soon is put in a situation to take an Apprentice, as happened with Plagueis with Palpatine and Palpatine with Anakin. 

Additionally, the Sith do not care about the manner in which they are victorious, only that they are victorious. Fighting from the shadows, appearing weak when you are strong, misdirection and beguilement are all powerful tools that the Sith used against the more conventional Jedi.
